summary: A 40-foot stone lookout on Rams Head in Medford, first operated 1916 and not used after 1918; only remains and stairs are visible today, per a visitor guide.

facts.status_note: Only the remains of the tower can be seen at the site today, including remaining stairs

access.note: Reached on foot by trails in Lawrence Woods, part of the Middlesex Fells Reservation; parking is generally limited

visit.trail_note: The hike up Rams Head to the remaining stairs is easy, with views of the surrounding cities and terrain

events.note: Register: first operated in 1916 (build date not given). Visitor guide credits a general and first mayor of Medford with building an observation tower on the hill

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 120 ft (37 m) for the site; visitor guide gives about 215 ft above sea level for the hill. Both kept in the story; the figures appear to measure different things and the sources do not say which applies to the tower base.

notes_for_editor: Register dates (1916-1918) and 'stone' construction are not contradicted by the guide, but the guide does not give a build year and credits the general with building the tower. An FFLAMASS Facebook search snippet describes a steel 'Lawrence Observatory' on Ram's Head used as a lookout from 1919; that conflicts with the register's stone tower and dates. The page could not be read, so nothing from it is cited or relied on; the editor may want to check it. Hill elevation 215 ft (guide) vs site 120 ft (register) is unresolved and is stated in the story as a conflict. Brief kind 'unknown' corrected to tower. The explorelocal guide is undated. Staffing: none found beyond 'used as a fire lookout'.
